q1: SELECT C.DEPT_NAME, SUM(I.SALARY) FROM COURSE AS C INNER JOIN DEPARTMENT AS D ON (C.DEPT_NAME = D.DEPT_NAME) INNER JOIN INSTRUCTOR AS I ON (D.DEPT_NAME = I.DEPT_NAME) GROUP BY C.DEPT_NAME HAVING SUM(I.SALARY) > 100 AND MAX(I.SALARY) < 75
q2: SELECT C.DEPT_NAME, SUM(I.SALARY) FROM COURSE AS C INNER JOIN DEPARTMENT AS D ON (C.DEPT_NAME = D.DEPT_NAME) INNER JOIN INSTRUCTOR AS I ON (D.DEPT_NAME = I.DEPT_NAME) GROUP BY C.DEPT_NAME HAVING SUM(I.SALARY) >= 100 AND MAX(I.SALARY) < 75

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent due to the difference in the SUM condition in the HAVING clause. Q1 uses SUM(I.SALARY) > 100 while Q2 uses SUM(I.SALARY) >= 100. This means Q2 will include groups where the sum is exactly 100, whereas Q1 will not. The MAX(I.SALARY) < 75 condition is the same in both queries.
